These appeals are filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'the M.V.Act').

2. MFA No.20713/2012, MFA No.20714/2012 and MFA No.20715/2012 are filed by the claimants challenging the common judgment and award dated 01.12.2011 passed in M.V.C. Nos.392/2011,
393/2011 and 395/2011 respectively by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-X, Bellary, (For short,
hereinafter
called
as 'Tribunal) seeking enhancement of compensation

. 
3. Brief facts of the case are that on 03.03.2009 at about 10.30 a.m. the appellant and other were proceeding to Sandur to attend the work in a Tata Indica Car bearing registration No.KA-34/M-5663 near Veniveerapura corss, at the same time lorry bearing registration No.MA-32/B- 3009 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the car and caused accident due to which appellant and others have sustained injuries.
Heard the arguments and perused the records.
In the present case, the accident was occurred on 03.03.2009.
The accident is between Truck and Car.
The claimants are occupants in the Indica Car.
Issue No.1 is answered by the Tribunal that the driver of the lorry has caused accident and he is solely responsible for the accident.
Ex.R.1 is driving license.

As per Ex.R.1-extract of driving license,
the driver of the lorry was holding driving license to drive LMV (non-transport).
The accident was caused on 03.03.2008.
As per Ex.R.1-license there is no endorsement either to drive heavy goods vehicle or heavy passenger vehicle, but only mentioned as transport vehicle.
Transport vehicle may be light motor vehicle or heavy goods vehicle or heavy passenger vehicle.
In the present case, the offending vehicle is truck, which is heavy goods vehicle.
But there is no mentioning in Ex.R.1 to drive heavy transport vehicle either truck or bus.

Today, the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submitted zerox copy of the driving license card in which it is NC:
2023:KHC-D:8913 mentioned the driver was having badge for driving the bus.
Even it is considered for driving bus of transport vehicle which is expired on 11.02.2003.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident, the driver of the lorry was not holding valid and affective driving license to drive the heavy goods vehicle.
In the present case, the Truck involved is heavy goods vehicle.
Therefore, it is proved that driver did not possess driving license to drive heavy goods vehicle.
Therefore, insurance company has successfully established its defence in rebutting the liability.
Regarding pay and recovery:
5. In the present case, the Tribunal has observed that driver of Lorry bearing registration No.MH-32/B-3009 had not possessed driving licence at the time of the accident.

Therefore, the Tribunal is correct in exonerating the Insurance Company Surendra S/O Thiruneelakanta vs Abdul Wahid S/O Abdul Majid on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178865687/
4 from paying compensation to the claimants.

sentences.text: However,

as per Sub-section (2) of Section 149 of Motor Vehicle Act, when the Insurance Company NC:
2023:KHC-D:8913 established the fact that driver was not holding driving license,
then as per Sub-sections (1), (5), (7) of Section 149 of Motor Vehicle Act, the Insurance Company as if the judgment debtor shall satisfy the claim in respect of third parties at the first instance and then recover the same from owner of the offending Lorry bearing registration No.MH-32/B-3009.

Accordingly, order of pay and recovery is made as per the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Pappu and Others vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another1;
National Insurance Company Limited vs. Swaran Singh and Others 2 and also as per the full bench decision of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited vs. Yellavva and Another3.

ii) Fracture of C-4 verbena seen with implants situ.
iii) Fracture of shoulder clavicle and injury to neck and forehead.

10. The Tribunal has awarded compensation under the head loss of amenities is found on lesser side.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.30,000/- is awarded under the head of amenities.

11. Further compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded under the head of 'attendant charges' like food,
nourishment etc.,
12.
The doctor stated that the claimant has suffered 50% of physical disability.
The claimant is civil engineer and the nature of work requires roaming in the field and inspection of civil engineer works.
Therefore, the fracture of Cervical Vertebra certainly causes effective future loss - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8913 of income and also effective future prospects in life.
Assessment of functional disability and physical disability are not based on mathematical formula.

The functional disability is to be assessed considering the age, nature of injury and disability occurred, the nature of work of the claimant and then how much said disability is affecting the nature of work of the claimant is to be assessed.
Therefore, it is always not mathematical formula to be considered.

Hence,
considering the fact that the claimant had suffered fracture of C-4 verbena and civil engineer by profession, it is just and proper to consider the functional disability at 25% towards whole body.
The accident was caused on 03.03.2009.
The Tribunal has held the income of the claimant has as Rs.7,500/- per month.
The claimant is Diploma in Civil Engineer holder, therefore, quite naturally the claimant must have been earning minimum of Rs.7,500/- per month and that is confirmed herein.
The claimant is aged 40 years.
The claimant has sustained significant injuries and disability as above discussed.

Therefore, certain income is added according to the age of the claimant towards loss of future prospects in life as per the judgment of the division bench of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Company vs. Abdul S/o Mehaboob Tahasildar4 and the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sidram vs. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Surendra S/O Thiruneelakanta vs Abdul Wahid S/O Abdul Majid on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178865687/

Brief facts of the case are that on 03.03.2009 at about 10.30 a.m. the appellant and other were proceeding to Sandur to attend the work in a Tata Indica Car bearing registration No.KA-34/M-5663 near Veniveerapura corss, at the same time lorry bearing registration No.MA-32/B- 3009 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the car and caused accident due to which appellant and others have sustained injuries.
opennyai_summary.facts:
In the present case, the accident was occurred on 03.03.2009.
The accident is between Truck and Car.
The claimants are occupants in the Indica Car.
Issue No.1 is answered by the Tribunal that the driver of the lorry has caused accident and he is solely responsible for the accident.
The accident was caused on 03.03.2008.
Transport vehicle may be light motor vehicle or heavy goods vehicle or heavy passenger vehicle.
In the present case, the offending vehicle is truck, which is heavy goods vehicle.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident, the driver of the lorry was not holding valid and affective driving license to drive the heavy goods vehicle.
In the present case, the Truck involved is heavy goods vehicle.
Therefore, it is proved that driver did not possess driving license to drive heavy goods vehicle.
Therefore, insurance company has successfully established its defence in rebutting the liability.
Therefore, the fracture of Cervical Vertebra certainly causes effective future loss - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8913 of income and also effective future prospects in life.
Assessment of functional disability and physical disability are not based on mathematical formula.
The functional disability is to be assessed considering the age, nature of injury and disability occurred, the nature of work of the claimant and then how much said disability is affecting the nature of work of the claimant is to be assessed.
Therefore, it is always not mathematical formula to be considered.
Hence,
considering the fact that the claimant had suffered fracture of C-4 verbena and civil engineer by profession, it is just and proper to consider the functional disability at 25% towards whole body.
The accident was caused on 03.03.2009.
The claimant is Diploma in Civil Engineer holder, therefore, quite naturally the claimant must have been earning minimum of Rs.7,500/- per month and that is confirmed herein.
The accident is occurred during the year 2009.
The Tribunal has correctly held functional disability at 10%.
The claimant was aged 40 years.

Accordingly, order of pay and recovery is made as per the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Pappu and Others vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another1;
National Insurance Company Limited vs. Swaran Singh and Others 2 and also as per the full bench decision of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited vs. Yellavva and Another3.
